title: Alphabet sounds, accents and clear introductions

questions.prompt: Which written form has an acute accent on e?
questions.explanation: École begins with é, which has an acute accent.

questions.prompt: Choose the correctly accented word for 'father'.
questions.explanation: The French word père contains a grave accent on è.

questions.prompt: Which French word includes a cedilla?
questions.explanation: Garçon uses ç before o to represent the /s/ sound.

questions.prompt: Select the spelling that uses a diaeresis.
questions.explanation: Noël uses ë to signal separate vowel sounds.

questions.prompt: Which French letter name is normally pronounced /ʒi/?
questions.explanation: The French name for J is pronounced /ʒi/; G is /ʒe/.

questions.prompt: Which French letter name is normally pronounced /ʒe/?
questions.explanation: The French name for G is /ʒe/, unlike the name for J.

questions.prompt: Which sequence spells the name 'Léa' letter by letter?
questions.explanation: Léa has the letter sequence L followed by É then A.

questions.prompt: Which French question asks how to spell a word?
questions.explanation: Comment ça s'écrit asks about spelling; se prononce asks pronunciation.

questions.prompt: Which sentence uses an accent to distinguish 'at/to' from 'has'?
questions.explanation: The preposition à bears a grave accent, unlike the verb form a.

questions.prompt: Read « Maëlle épelle son prénom. » What is Maëlle doing?
questions.explanation: Épeller means to spell a word aloud, and prénom means first name.

questions.prompt: Read « Sur le badge, il y a écrit Élodie. » What does the badge show?
questions.explanation: The text says the name Élodie is written on the badge.

questions.prompt: Read « Tu peux répéter plus lentement ? » What does the speaker request?
questions.explanation: Répéter plus lentement asks somebody to say it again more slowly.

questions.prompt: Read « Le mot français commence par F. » Which letter begins français?
questions.explanation: Commence par F explicitly identifies the initial letter.

questions.prompt: Read « Il faut ajouter un accent sur le e. » What is missing?
choices: An extra letter at the end.
An accent on the letter e.
questions.explanation: Ajouter un accent sur le e means add an accent mark to e.

questions.prompt: Read « Je m'appelle Anaïs. » Which mark is visible in the name?
questions.explanation: Anaïs is written with a diaeresis on the letter i.

questions.prompt: Read « Mon nom de famille est Dupont. » Which information follows?
questions.explanation: Nom de famille means surname or family name.

questions.prompt: Read « Écrivez votre prénom en majuscules. » What should the learner do?
choices: Write the first name in capital letters.
questions.explanation: En majuscules specifies uppercase or capital letters.

questions.prompt: Read « Je n'ai pas compris la dernière lettre. » What was difficult?
questions.explanation: Dernière lettre refers to the final letter in a sequence.

questions.prompt: A teacher says your name too quickly. Which reply helps without interrupting rudely?
choices: Pouvez-vous répéter plus lentement, s'il vous plaît ?
questions.explanation: Pouvez-vous and s'il vous plaît form a polite request for slower repetition.

questions.prompt: You want to ask a classmate to spell their name. Which is appropriate?
questions.explanation: Épeler means to spell; ton prénom means your first name.

questions.prompt: A student writes 'ecole' but the model reads 'école'. Which revision is needed?
choices: Replace the o with a u.
Add an acute accent to the first e.
Add a cedilla to the final e.
questions.explanation: École requires an acute accent on its initial e.

questions.prompt: You need to spell 'Noël' on a registration form. Which entry is exact?
questions.explanation: The diaeresis belongs on the e in Noël, not on the o.

questions.prompt: You must introduce yourself clearly to a new teacher. Which two sentences work together?
choices: Salut, je suis lundi. I – N – E – S.
Bonsoir, il s'appelle Inès. I – E – N – S.
Bonjour, je m'appelle Inès. I – N – È – S.
questions.explanation: The first option gives an introduction and preserves the accent and letter order.

questions.prompt: You heard « G » but wrote « J » during a spelling exercise. What should you check?
choices: Whether neither letter has a French name.
Whether both letter names end in /a/.
questions.explanation: G and J begin similarly, but their French names use different vowel sounds.

questions.prompt: You want to check the pronunciation rather than the written spelling. What do you ask?
questions.explanation: Se prononce asks how a word is pronounced, unlike s'écrit.

questions.prompt: A student writes « Je vais a la bibliothèque ». Which correction is justified?
questions.explanation: The preposition à takes a grave accent in standard French spelling.

questions.prompt: A classmate says « Je m'appelle Chloé ». What is the best verification question if you missed the spelling?
choices: Tu peux traduire ta ville, s'il te plaît ?
Tu peux épeler Chloé, s'il te plaît ?
Tu peux changer de prénom, s'il te plaît ?
questions.explanation: Asking someone to spell their name directly addresses uncertainty about letters.
